<Heading
  as={"h1"}
  className={"openapi__heading"}
  children={"Receive a new order — allocates and releases automatically"}
>
</Heading>

<MethodEndpoint
  method={"post"}
  path={"/orders"}
  context={"endpoint"}
>
  
</MethodEndpoint>



Intake — the ReceiveOrder use case. Validates every requested line (SKU non-empty, quantity > 0), mints an `OrderId`, and persists the order in `Received` status, publishing `OrderReceived` unconditionally.

Immediately afterward, in the SAME call, this service attempts allocation-then-release: it reserves stock per line via inventory-storage's `POST /reservations` (see the Allocation tag), and for every line that ends up `Allocated` and eligible under BR3 (see below), releases it — announced via the enriched `OrderAllocated` / `OrderPartiallyAllocated` Kafka events, never a second synchronous call. If that implicit allocation attempt hits a hard (non-business) failure, this endpoint still returns `201`: the order genuinely was received, and a caller expressing "place an order" must never be told that failed just because an internal, best-effort next step could not complete. The returned body reflects whatever the allocation pass actually achieved.

`allowPartialShipment` defaults to `false` — ship-complete (BR3). Every line's `pathId` is chosen by this service, not the caller (ADR 0021): the active process paths in the process-path catalogue are filtered by their declared eligibility and the shortest known cycle time wins (ties: lower path id), falling back to the default `pick` when no catalogue is configured or no path is active. A caller placing an order has no business supplying wes-work-planning's process-path vocabulary at intake; `pathId` is visible on every line in the response, but not settable on the request.

Idempotent (REST guideline, ADR 0023/0048): send an `Idempotency-Key` header. A retry with the same key, method, path and body replays the stored answer (with `Idempotency-Replayed: true`) and creates no second order; the same key with another body is 409 `idempotency-key-reused`.

It applies to ordinary orders and to a network-originated hold (`releaseOnAllocation: false`, ADR 0020) alike.\n\nWhen present it is stored on the order, immutable for its lifetime (re-promise, release and cancel never change it), and is the site of every `SiteSkuDemandChanged` event for the order's lines (`assignment_version` `order-site-v1`, ADR 0044). It is also the site the order is PROMISED against (ADR 0047): the CPT window comes from that site's CPT schedule, at intake and on every re-promise, and the `capacityConstraint` annotation matches that site. A site with no CPT schedule known to this service is promised on the `LeadTime` basis, never on another site's windows. When absent the order behaves exactly as before: it is promised against the deployment's default site (`DEFAULT_SITE_ID`) and demand projects to the deployment's static site, if one is configured (`static-site-v1`, ADR 0035). The frozen `OrderAllocated` / `OrderPartiallyAllocated` / `OrderRepromised` events never carry it. An externally-dictated deadline (RFC 3339) — the instant this order must ship by, set by someone other than this service (a retail network's required ship-by, for example).\n\nWhen present the promise is CONSTRAINED to a CPT window at or before it, rather than being the earliest window this service can manage; specifically, the LATEST window that still meets the deadline is chosen, leaving the floor maximum slack (ADR 0020 §2). When the deadline cannot be met the order is still created and allocated, but comes back with NO `promiseDate` at all — an absent promise is the honest signal that we cannot commit, and is exactly what a caller holding a fill-or-kill obligation needs to see before acknowledging it downstream.\n\nUnlike the ordinary promise path, this one has NO lead-time fallback: missing schedule or capability data yields no promise rather than an estimate, because a guess dressed as a commitment is worse than an admission of ignorance.\n"},"releaseOnAllocation":{"type":"boolean","default":true,"description":"When true (the default, and the behaviour of every caller that omits the field), the order is received, allocated and released in one call exactly as before ADR 0020. When false the order is HELD: lines are allocated, inventory reservations genuinely exist and a promise is computed and attached, but nothing is released and no work reaches the floor until `POST /orders/{id}/releases`. Intended for a caller that must decide whether to commit to the order before it becomes work — see ADR 0020. A held order must be ship-complete: sending `releaseOnAllocation: false` together with `allowPartialShipment: true` is rejected with `422`.\n"},"allowPartialShipment":{"type":"boolean","default":false,"description":"When false (the default — ship-complete, BR3), a single backordered line holds the WHOLE order back from release until an allocation retry (`POST /orders/{id}/allocation-retries`) clears it.
